title: Listenability of Synthetic Speech: On the Effect of Linguistic Registers in Text-to-Speech Input
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), LLM-generated text is increasingly being used as input for speech synthesis, yet little is known about its listenability compared to other linguistic registers. This paper presents a preliminary study of listenability across conversational, formal written, simplified written, and LLM-generated registers in terms of listener effort and comprehension during synthesized delivery. An experiment with 47 participants measured subjective mental effort, cognitive load, and cued recall in a within-subjects design. Register characteristics were examined through readability metrics and Biber's Multi-Dimensional Analysis. Our findings indicate higher listenability for synthesized speech from written sources compared to radio transcripts, demonstrating the intricacies of language and register. Furthermore, LLM-generated text was as listenable as Wikipedia-sourced text, supporting its suitability in synthetic speech applications.
relevance_note: Listener study of synthesized-speech listenability across text registers including LLM-generated input; evaluation of TTS output with human listeners.
